ION attributes the poor performance of MEA at ENTP to the significant foaming that occurred in the stripper. 9.2 ICE-21™ ION operated for 1167 hours from October 2023 to February 2024 with ICE-21™. From October 2023 to December 2023, ION performed 350 hours of parametric testing. ION switched to continuous 24-hour operations in December 2023. Following parametric testing, ION performed 817 hours of long-term testing until February 2024. The ENTP plant was shut down over Thanksgiving for a power plant outage. The ENTP plant was also shut down during the second half of December 2023 due to a malfunctioning variable frequency drive (VFD) on the flue gas blower. All setpoints were run at water neutral flue gas temperatures because the DCC blowdown was not permitted for discharge. During standard operations, the DCC condenses water out of the flue gas stream to cool it to the setpoint, and the condensed water is blown down out of the DCC. However, with no DCC blowdown, the flue gas could only be cooled to its dew point, meaning that the flue gas entered the absorber at high temperatures (>115 °F) compared to the design point (95 °F). At lower flue gas temperatures, the equilibrium for CO absorption into the solvent is more favorable 2 as CO absorption is an exothermic reaction. In addition, the lower flue gas temperature results in 2 lower rich solvent temperatures, thus more heat can be recovered in the lean rich heat exchanger, improving the overall efficiency of the process and lowering SRD.
